reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.

consistencyRules.message: Rotation is not assessed when a high-risk factor is present.
Rotation is only assessed when at least one low-risk factor allows safe assessment.

commonErrors: Testing rotation before excluding high-risk factors.
Applying to patients with GCS below 15.
name: Canadian C-spine Rule

version.label: Canadian C-spine Rule (Stiell et al. 2001)
version.detail: Three steps: any high-risk factor → radiography; no low-risk factor → radiography; low-risk factor present → assess active rotation 45° left and right; unable → radiography.

purpose: Identifies alert, stable trauma patients in whom the rule's criteria for cervical spine imaging are met.
intendedPopulation: Alert (GCS 15), stable adults (16+) after blunt trauma to the head or neck.

calculatorNotice.title: Check that the rule applies
calculatorNotice.message: Not for children, GCS below 15, unstable vital signs, penetrating trauma, acute paralysis, known vertebral disease or previous cervical spine surgery.

options.label: Yes: alert, stable adult with blunt head or neck trauma

inputDefinitions.label: Dangerous mechanism
inputDefinitions.help: Fall from 3 feet / 1 m or 5 stairs; axial load to the head; motor vehicle collision at high speed (>100 km/h), rollover or ejection; motorised recreational vehicle; bicycle collision.

inputDefinitions.label: Simple rear-end motor vehicle collision
inputDefinitions.help: Excludes being pushed into oncoming traffic, hit by a bus or large truck, rollover, or hit by a high-speed vehicle.

inputDefinitions.label: Sitting position in the emergency department
Ambulatory at any time since injury
Absence of midline cervical spine tenderness
Able to actively rotate the neck 45° to the left and right?
inputDefinitions.help: Only assessed when no high-risk factor and at least one low-risk factor is present.

calculationMethod.display: {total == 0 ? 'Not applicable' : total == 1 ? 'Rule criteria not met' : total == 4 ? 'Assess rotation' : 'Rule criteria met'}
calculationMethod.share: Canadian C-spine Rule: {total == 0 ? 'not applicable' : total == 1 ? 'low risk, able to rotate 45°' : total == 2 ? 'high-risk factor' : total == 3 ? 'no low-risk factor' : total == 4 ? 'rotation not yet assessed' : 'unable to rotate 45°'}

resultStates.label: Rule not applicable
resultStates.summary: The patient is outside the population in which the rule was derived.
resultStates.detail: Use clinical judgement and local protocol.

resultStates.label: High-risk factor present
resultStates.summary: A high-risk factor is present: the rule's criteria for radiography are met.
resultStates.detail: Assess according to the clinical situation and local protocol.

resultStates.label: No low-risk factor
resultStates.summary: No low-risk factor allows safe assessment of range of motion: the rule's criteria for radiography are met.

resultStates.label: Assess active rotation
resultStates.summary: A low-risk factor is present. Assess whether the patient can actively rotate the neck 45° left and right.

resultStates.label: Unable to rotate 45°
resultStates.summary: Unable to actively rotate the neck 45° left and right: the rule's criteria for radiography are met.

resultStates.label: Rule criteria not met
resultStates.summary: No high-risk factor, a low-risk factor present and able to rotate 45° left and right: the rule's criteria for radiography are not met.

clinicalContext.text: High sensitivity and better specificity than NEXUS in the head-to-head validation study.

clinicalInsights.text: Active rotation is assessed only after a low-risk factor makes it safe.

limitations.text: Only for alert, stable adults; excluded groups need clinical judgement.

whatItDoesNotTellYou: Head injury risk (see Canadian CT Head Rule).

guideSections.what: A three-step rule for cervical spine radiography in alert, stable trauma patients.
guideSections.whenToUse: Alert (GCS 15), stable adults after blunt head or neck trauma.
guideSections.howToPerform: 1) Any high-risk factor → criteria met. 2) If no low-risk factor → criteria met. 3) Otherwise ask the patient to rotate 45° each way; unable → criteria met.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Supports, but does not replace, clinical judgement.

sources.citation: Stiell IG, Wells GA, Vandemheen KL, et al. The Canadian C-spine rule for radiography in alert and stable trauma patients. JAMA. 2001;286(15):1841-1848.
Stiell IG, Clement CM, McKnight RD, et al. The Canadian C-spine rule versus the NEXUS low-risk criteria in patients with trauma. N Engl J Med. 2003;349(26):2510-2518.
